This appeal coming on for admission this day, the court  the following:
 JUDGEMENT Heard finally, with the consent of the parties.

2] This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellants under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 20.12.2022, passed by Second Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.) in Claim Case No.819/2022 whereby, a sum of Rs.16,20,000/- has been awarded to the appellants on account of death of Arjun Rathore.

3] In brief, the facts of the case are that the deceased Arjun Rathore met with an accident on 30.12.2021, when he was going on his motorcycle bearing registration No.MP-09-VW-6176, and when he reached at Badgonda road, near Balaji Temple, Indore, a car bearing registration No.MP-09-CC-7920, being driven rashly and negligently by the respondent No.3, dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased from rear side, as a result of which he suffered grievous injuries, and died on the spot only.
Subsequently, a claim case was filed by the appellants on the ground that the deceased was earning Rs.18,000/- per month as a driver and thus, an amount of Rs.70,00,000/-
was claimed.
The learned MACT, after recording the evidence, has awarded a sum of Rs.16,20,000/-, considering the income of the deceased to be Rs.7,000/- per month.

4] Counsel for the appellants has submitted that the income of the deceased was Rs.18,000/- per month, which is proved by Ex.P-35, which clearly indicates that the deceased was earning Rs.18,000/- per month.

5] Counsel for the respondent, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that the certificate has not been proved in accordance with law, and the employer of the deceased has not been examined by the appellants.
Thus, it is submitted that no case for interference is made out.
6] Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.

7] Having considered rival submissions, on perusal of the record, and also considering the fact that the deceased was taking care of as many as six dependants, including his wife the appellant No.1, his minor children aged 8 to 13 years,
appellant Nos.2 to 4, and his parents appellants No.5 and 6

. In such circumstances, it cannot be said that he was surviving on the income of Rs.7,000/- only, and in the facts and circumstances of the case, as per the revised guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority, his income can be considered as Rs.8,800/- per month, and the assessment can be made accordingly.
